messages:
secret-scan-bot: automated paste scanner flagged a possible production API token in https://pastebin.com/xyZ9Ab1 (pattern match sk-prod-...). severity: medium-high.
angela: grabbing the paste now. can someone check key registry for that suffix?
matt: @angela share in DM once confirmed. if it's prod, we need immediate revoke + rotation.
angela: pasted to eng-security-priv. match looks like sk-prod-9c4d7e2f which maps to key-id: d9e7c4b1 in secrets registry. created by service-account ingestion-runner.
eli: tagging infra-oncall. please stage containment steps: disable key d9e7c4b1, issue replacement, and throttle any traffic using that key.
infra-oncall: on it. disabling now. will also add temporary ACL to block IPs seen in the paste metadata. ETA ~8m.
angela: containment steps I'm taking: 1) revoke d9e7c4b1, 2) issue new key d9e7c4b2, 3) update CI pipelines that reference the old key, 4) run token usage lookup for last 7 days.
matt: share the token usage query for logs so sec-ops can run customer impact checks.
eli: use these:
```
index=prod-requests api_key.id=d9e7c4b1 | stats count by client_id, src.ip, route
```
and in EventDB:
```
SELECT ts, client_id, route, src_ip FROM token_events WHERE key_id='d9e7c4b1' AND ts > now() - interval '7 days';
```
angela: quick RBAC check: the key has role set ingest:write and model:invoke. no admin or cross-tenant privileges.
lina: good. still need to enumerate which customers (client_id) may have had requests via that key. angela, can you export client list and send to sec-comms & legal over secure channel?
angela: exporting now. preliminary results: 9 distinct client_ids in last 48h, 2 enterprise-tier clients with higher volumes. sending encrypted file to legal and SOC.
infra-oncall: revocation finished. new key rolled into pipelines for staging; prod rollout in progress with health checks. WAF rule applied to block the suspicious IPs and ips with rapid request rates.
secret-scan-bot: added paste URL to high-priority watchlist and added new fingerprint rule for tokens emitted by ingestion-runner.
matt: KMS question: was raw key material exposed or just derived API token? eli, can you confirm with auth-service and KMS audit?
eli: checked KMS logs: service-account private key material remained in KMS. the leaked string is a bearer token minted by auth-service at 2026-03-12T15:04:11Z by deploy pipeline. creation event logged.
angela: side note: one CI job in pipeline prints token metadata to build logs; there was an unmerged PR to remove it. opening an emergency PR to remove any printing and re-run the job to scrub logs.
matt: add a CI gate to fail if any env var contains sk-prod- or matches token regex. also add masking for any printed values matching token patterns.
angela: added to SEC-705 and SEC-706 tickets: SEC-705 (rotate & revoke audit trail), SEC-706 (CI log sanitization + gate). ETA for CI changes: 48h.
lina: customer comms plan: wait until we confirm data exfiltration. legal wants a heads-up to the two enterprise clients with an offer to rotate their integration keys and a summary of containment actions. I'll draft a short factual note.
legal: please include timelines and the specific mitigations; do not speculate about data loss. we'll review the client list and advise on notification thresholds.
eli: recommended post-incident actions: 1) enforce 90-day rotation for service tokens, 2) remove unnecessary model:invoke permission from ingestion-runner, 3) add token age alert (tokens older than 30d with any high-throughput usage), 4) broaden paste scanner patterns.
infra-oncall: RBAC change requires migration; scheduling a safe rollout window. estimated 5 days for permission contraction across services.
angela: creating tickets for each recommendation: SEC-707 (rotation policy), SEC-708 (RBAC permission tightening), SEC-709 (token age alerts), SEC-710 (scanner expansion). owners assigned.
secret-scan-bot: raising severity to P1 until customer impact verification completes. :rotating_light: reactions from several folks.
matt: one more: run a historical paste sweep for common token patterns and our service-account prefixes. liaise with OSINT team if needed.
angela: sweep started. initial sweep found 2 older pastes with different token IDs; those keys were already rotated by routine cadence.
lina: I'll hold off on client emails until we confirm whether any customer data was accessed. target update in 3 hours or sooner.
matt: thanks team — quick work on containment. keep updates in this thread. we'll do a short incident review after tickets are triaged. :thumbsup:
